transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you that made you decide to seek help today?

Well, I... I came in because I keep catching myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn't wake up. I haven't made any plans to hurt myself or anything, it's just this thought that creeps in. Like the other day, I was at work—I work in retail, you know, over at the hardware store on 5th—and I was stocking these new hammers. We used to carry the ones with the wooden handles, but now everything is fiberglass. People say it absorbs the shock better, but I don't know, there's something about the weight of a good wooden hammer, you know? My grandfather had this old wooden one he used to build his shed... anyway, yeah, I just keep having these thoughts about not waking up.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like working on projects like your grandfather's shed?

Yeah, I... I guess so. It's funny you mention the shed, because I haven't picked up a tool in weeks. It's like... well, a while back I had this week where I was just going, going, going. I rearranged the whole stockroom at work, painted the living room, didn't even need to sleep much. But after that burst of energy wore off, it felt like somebody had just pulled the plug on me. 

I'd wake up and just sit at the kitchen table, staring at my coffee. Just feeling so... empty. And ashamed, though I don't even know what I'm ashamed of. My wife bought this new coffee maker, one of those fancy ones that grinds the beans right there. She got a great deal on it at that big box store out by the highway, the one that used to be a bowling alley? I used to bowl in a league there back in the nineties. We were called the Pin Pals... clever, right? We won the championship in '98. But yeah, these days, I just sit there while the machine whirs, and I don't even care about drinking the coffee. I just feel drained.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy, like bowling with your league or working on projects?

Yeah, I have. I just quit caring about the things that usually settle me down. Like, I used to love going fishing out at the reservoir, or digging through crates of vinyl records at that shop downtown... you know the one, right next to the diner that makes those huge milkshakes? They use real ice cream, not that soft-serve stuff. I took my nephew there once, and he couldn't even finish a small. Anyway, I used to love all that, or tailgating before the games, or even just checking on my home-brew setup in the basement. But lately... I don't know, it all just feels like chores. Like too much effort. I haven't even checked the airlock on my latest batch of stout, and it's probably ruined by now. My buddy Dave got me into brewing. He's an engineer, so he gets really technical with the temperatures and all that... but yeah, I just don't have the energy for it anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way — this lack of interest and feeling drained — for most of the day, nearly every day?

Well, let's see... this whole low spell, it's been hanging on for about three months now. Ever since I had that crash after all that energy I told you about. Three months is a long time, you know? It's funny, three months is exactly how long it took my brother-in-law to rebuild the transmission on his '69 Mustang. He thought he could do it in a weekend, but he kept ordering the wrong parts. He gets his parts from this catalog company out in California, and their shipping takes forever. I told him he should just go to the local auto parts store, the one with the big neon sign shaped like a spark plug. The guy who runs it, Sal, he knows everything about classic Fords. His dad opened the place back in the fifties. But no, my brother-in-law had to use the catalog... anyway, yeah, it's been about three months of feeling like this most days.

Have you ever experienced a period of time when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or so confident that you didn’t need much sleep, maybe even acting impulsively or unusually fast-paced in your thoughts or actions?

Yeah, actually. It's... well, right after I got fired from the hardware store, I didn't feel down at all. I felt oddly fired up, like I was going to prove everybody wrong. I had all these ideas about starting my own business. I was going to open a specialty tool shop, you know, catering to the real craftsmen. The kind of guys who appreciate a good hand plane. My grandfather had this old Stanley Bailey No. 4 smoothing plane, beautiful piece of equipment. Rosewood handles, cast iron body. He used to keep it oiled and wrapped in a soft cloth in his toolbox. I still have it, actually, sitting on a shelf in the garage. I should probably check on it, make sure it's not rusting... 

But yeah, I was so energized, but I was also... I don't know, irritable? Like, I remember being at the coffee shop downtown, the one with the exposed brick walls, and I was just snapping at people over the littlest things. The barista took too long with my order, and I just went off on her. Which isn't like me. I usually tip well. They have these really good blueberry scones there, too. They bake them fresh every morning. You have to get there before nine if you want one, otherwise they sell out. The owner, he used to be a baker in the Navy, so he knows what he's doing. But yeah, I was just so wound up and snapping at everybody.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where you felt so good, energetic, or invincible that others noticed you were acting unusually, or it led to risky behavior?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean, during that same time when I was all fired up about the tool shop, I had this... this feeling like I was just unstoppable. For a while I honestly believed I could walk into any hardware store in the whole district and run it better than the managers there. Like somehow losing my job had made me the ultimate expert on retail. I was ready to just walk into the Home Depot out on Route 9 and start giving orders. That Home Depot, by the way, they reorganized their plumbing aisle last year and it’s a total disaster now. You can't find the PVC fittings to save your life. I was trying to fix a leak under my kitchen sink—just a simple P-trap replacement, you know? But I had to go to three different aisles just to get the right primer and cement. The guy working there, a young kid, maybe nineteen, had no clue what I was asking for. He kept pointing me toward the garden hoses. Kids these days don't know the first thing about basic home repair. They don't teach shop class in high school anymore, which is a real shame. My shop teacher, Mr. Henderson, he was missing half his left index finger from a band saw accident, but he could build a birdhouse blindfolded. Anyway, yeah, I felt like I was invincible, like I knew more than anyone else running those stores.
